# dupl

**dupl** is a tool for finding code clones in Go source files.

## Usage

```
Usage of dupl:
  dupl [flags] [paths]

Paths:
  If the given path is a file, dupl will use it regardless of
  the file extension. If it is a directory it will recursively
  search for *.go files in that directory.

  If no path is given dupl will recursively search for *.go
  files in the current directory.

Flags:
  -files
        read file names from stdin one at each line
  -html
        output the results as HTML, including duplicate code fragments
  -plumbing
        plumbing (easy-to-parse) output for consumption by scripts or tools
  -t, -threshold size
        minimum token sequence size as a clone (default 15)
  -vendor
        check files in vendor directory
  -v, -verbose
        explain what is being done

Examples:
  dupl -t 100
        Search clones in the current directory of size at least
        100 tokens.
  dupl $(find app/ -name '*_test.go')
        Search for clones in tests in the app directory.
  find app/ -name '*_test.go' |dupl -files
        The same as above.
```

```bash
$ dupl -t 200 -html >docker.html
```

// ParseFile parses the named Go file and converts it.
func ParseFile(name string) (*tree.Node, error) {
	fset := token.NewFileSet()
	f, err := parser.ParseFile(fset, name, nil, 0)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	c := &converter{fset: fset, name: name}
	return c.conv(f), nil
}

type converter struct {
	fset *token.FileSet
	name string
}

func (c *converter) offset(p token.Pos) int {
	return c.fset.File(p).Offset(p)
}

func (c *converter) conv(an ast.Node) *tree.Node {
	n := &tree.Node{File: c.name}
	n.Start = c.offset(an.Pos())
	n.Stop = c.offset(an.End())

	switch x := an.(type) {
	case *ast.ArrayType:
		n.Kind = kArrayType
		if x.Len != nil {
			n.Add(c.conv(x.Len))
		}
		n.Add(c.conv(x.Elt))

	case *ast.AssignStmt:
		n.Kind = kAssignStmt
		for i := len(x.Rhs) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
			n.Add(c.conv(x.Rhs[i]))
		}
		for _, e := range x.Lhs {
			n.Add(c.conv(e))
		}

	case *ast.BasicLit:
		n.Kind = kBasicLit

	case *ast.BinaryExpr:
		n.Kind = kBinaryExpr
		n.Add(c.conv(x.X), c.conv(x.Y))

	case *ast.BlockStmt:
		n.Kind = kBlockStmt
		for _, s := range x.List {
			n.Add(c.conv(s))
		}

	case *ast.BranchStmt:
		n.Kind = kBranchStmt
		if x.Label != nil {
			n.Add(c.conv(x.Label))
		}

	case *ast.CallExpr:
		n.Kind = kCallExpr
		n.Add(c.conv(x.Fun))
		for _, a := range x.Args {
			n.Add(c.conv(a))
		}

	case *ast.CaseClause:
		n.Kind = kCaseClause
		for _, e := range x.List {
			n.Add(c.conv(e))
		}
		for _, s := range x.Body {
			n.Add(c.conv(s))
		}

	case *ast.ChanType:
		n.Kind = kChanType
		n.Add(c.conv(x.Value))

	case *ast.CommClause:
		n.Kind = kCommClause
		if x.Comm != nil {
			n.Add(c.conv(x.Comm))
		}

		}

	case *ast.CompositeLit:
		n.Kind = kCompositeLit
		if x.Type != nil {

		}

		}

		n.Add(c.conv(x.Call))

	dst      *node

	suffix *node

// Tree is a suffix tree built incrementally token by token.

	toks   []int
	root   *node
	bottom *node // auxiliary state above the root
	act    *node
	k      int
}

// New returns an empty tree.
func New() *Tree {
	t := &Tree{root: &node{}, bottom: &node{}}
	t.root.suffix = t.bottom
	t.act = t.root
	return t

	for _, e := range s.edges {
		if t.toks[e.from] == tok {
